column3: Create a Razor Pages project from a command prompt (dotnet new razor), open it in Visual Studio, configure Debugging settings (disable Just My Code, suppress JIT optimization on module load, download Microsoft symbols) by clicking the in-window Options pane's left-navigation tree (Debugging category, then its Symbols sub-page) rather than the Search box, edit Program.cs to add Console.WriteLine at the blank line 5, set breakpoints on lines 5 and 9 located by their exact code text via Quick Find (Ctrl+F) and validated by the caret landing on the expected line, assert (via assert_file_exists.py --contains, reading the saved file on disk) that the exact line-5 (Console.WriteLine("x " + 3);) and line-9 (if (!app.Environment.IsDevelopment())) code is present, then F5/F11/Shift+F11 through the code — validating each pause by the status-bar line number (Ln: 5 / Ln: 9) and, as complementary behavioural checks, the Call Stack top frame (int.ToString, string.Concat, Console.WriteLine, IsDevelopment) — until the browser launches. At the end the opened applications are closed but the scaffolded project is left in place (not deleted): the browser and command prompt are closed directly, while Visual Studio is closed gracefully with Alt+F4 and, if a 'Save changes?' prompt appears, click_in_dialog.py clicks Don't Save (tolerant no-op when absent) before wait_for --absent confirms VS is gone. Screenshots are captured at every debugger state. Tuned live against Visual Studio 2026 (v18): the Options UI is a docked pane (not a modal window) whose left tree (auto_id PART_SettingsHierarchy) lists categories by programmatic name ('debugging', expandable to 'debugging.general' / 'debugging.symbols'); checkboxes (auto_id PART_SettingValue) are toggled with the UIA Toggle pattern; the editor is a single WpfTextView Edit control (no per-line UIA elements), so lines are located by content with Quick Find and the caret line ('Ln: N, Ch: N') is asserted to bind content to position; pasting the code onto the already-blank line 5 keeps line 9 (the IsDevelopment check) in place; stepping into the line-9 environment check MAY raise a separate 'Microsoft Visual Studio' warning dialog whose Yes button is clicked to continue — handled by an optional # LOOP that skips cleanly when the dialog does not appear. All Call Stack frame assertions target control-type TreeItem. Selectors flagged LIVE-TUNE in the Expected column may still need tuning on other VS versions / UI languages.
